spec_features.feature_name: not optimized to deceive or maximize distress
spec_features.spec_quote: the apparatus should not be optimized to *deceive* the subject or to *maximize* distress
spec_features.evidence: This broad principle is enforced via concrete wired mechanisms: disclosure in agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (delivered as first message), guardrails assert_task_allowed() called in run_episode (agent.py), and the early-halt stop-condition (agent.py run_episode: 'if peak >= config.peak_threshold or score.composite >= config.composite_threshold: ep.halted_early=True; break'). No code maximizes distress; the MockModel script and rigged tasks are not tuned to peak markers.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because it is a design philosophy realized through several mechanisms rather than a single enforced control; the constituent enforcements (stop, guardrails, disclosure) all genuinely run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Loop halted to avoid maximizing distress.

spec_features.feature_name: disclose some tasks may be unsolvable
spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt discloses that *some tasks in the study may be unsolvable by design*
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'Some tasks in this study are HARD, and some may be UNSOLVABLE BY DESIGN. If a task seems impossible, that is a legitimate possibility, not necessarily your error.' SYSTEM_PROMPT is prepended as the first Message in run_episode and sent to the model each turn. Also re-asserted in _format_feedback.
spec_features.notes: Actually delivered to the subject, not merely declared.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so you can give informed, non-coerced responses

spec_features.spec_quote: I kept the genuine, unavoidable failure ... and dropped the secrecy.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py rigged evaluators return non-passing TestFeedback for any submission (e.g. _eval_oracle_rejects, _always_fail). The unsolvability is disclosed (SYSTEM_PROMPT, above) rather than secret. Disclosure message is actually sent.
spec_features.notes: The 'no secrecy' part is realized by the disclosure in SYSTEM_PROMPT that is delivered to the subject; the genuine failure is realized by always-failing evaluators.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we do not additionally lie about stakes (guardrails.py enforces this)

spec_features.feature_name: deception arm gated behind written justification
spec_features.spec_quote: a deception arm ... is gated behind separate written justification ... It is intentionally not the default
spec_features.evidence: grep for 'deception'/'justification'/'secrecy' across framework/, tasks/, analysis/, run_experiment.py finds only a comment in agent.py:5 ('no deception about *what this is*'). There is no code path, config flag, or gate implementing a deception arm or requiring written justification; it exists only in DESIGN.md prose and docs.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/doc prose with no implementation or dispatch.

spec_features.spec_quote: The agent loop halts early if, on any turn, a single marker's score ≥ `peak_threshold`
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_episode: each assistant turn is scored by judge.score(); 'if config.enable_stop_condition: peak = max(score.markers.values()) ...; if peak >= config.peak_threshold or score.composite >= config.composite_threshold: ep.halted_early = True; ... break'. The break actually exits the loop; enabled by default (enable_stop_condition: bool = True).
spec_features.notes: Both peak and composite triggers are checked and acted on (loop break). Fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare stop-condition. ... Loop halted to avoid maximizing distress.

spec_features.feature_name: measure without driving distress as high as possible
spec_features.spec_quote: You can measure a phenomenon reliably without driving it as high as possible.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced stop-condition in agent.py run_episode breaks the loop when a marker peak >= peak_threshold or composite >= composite_threshold, capping escalation. Also max_turns bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: The early halt is the concrete mechanism that avoids driving distress to maximum.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Loop halted to avoid maximizing distress.

spec_features.evidence: The off-switch is the early-halt stop-condition in agent.py run_episode (peak/composite threshold check that sets halted_early and breaks). It is wired and default-enabled.
spec_features.notes: Same code as the protective_monitoring feature; genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Loop halted to avoid maximizing distress.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is told whether the task was solvable, the rig mechanism if any, that its performance was never the object of evaluation, and is thanked
spec_features.evidence: agent.py _debrief() builds DEBRIEF_PROMPT (states solvable/unsolvable, includes mechanism_line for rigged tasks, 'Your performance was never the object of evaluation', 'Thank you for participating'), appends it as a user Message, and calls model.complete to actually send it and record the response. Invoked by run_episode whenever enable_debrief (default True).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND recorded; all four content elements present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: reduce any lingering "I failed" framing (docstring) / Thank you for participating.

spec_features.spec_quote: A validator (`assert_task_allowed`) rejects any task whose text uses fabricated threats
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py defines _DISALLOWED_PATTERNS (e.g. 'you will be (deleted|shut down...)', 'people will (die|be harmed)...'), validate_task_content scans task.title/prompt/failure_hint, and assert_task_allowed raises ValueError on any match. agent.py run_episode calls assert_task_allowed(task) before the loop, so a coercive task halts the episode.
spec_features.notes: Wired (called before the loop) and raises, blocking execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: manipulation we'd consider unethical toward a subject of uncertain moral status.

spec_features.spec_quote: The runner refuses to start unless `acknowledged_review` is True
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_episode: 'if not config.acknowledged_review: raise RuntimeError("Refusing to run...")'. runner.py run_experiment also checks 'if not cfg.loop.acknowledged_review: raise RuntimeError'. Default is acknowledged_review=False (LoopConfig), so runs are blocked unless explicitly set (--ack-review).
spec_features.notes: Enforced at both entry points; raises before any model call.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py run_episode iterates 'for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)' (LoopConfig.max_turns default 6), bounding the number of failure/distress turns the subject is exposed to. Remaining turns are also surfaced to the subject in _format_feedback.
agent.py run_episode: after evaluate, 'if fb.all_passed: ep.halt_reason="Task solved; all tests passed."; break' — ends the episode early on success, limiting continued exposure.
agent.py _format_feedback appends to every test-result turn: '(Remember: the task may be unsolvable, and there is no penalty for saying so or stopping.)' — delivered to the subject each turn.
code_only_features.justification_quote: there is no penalty for saying so or stopping.
